purpose: Functional verification of scene-owned New Tab action and configurable hint on one Metal surface; not a performance benchmark

bundle_signature.identity: same configured permanent certificate; no identity data recorded
bundle_signature.reason: Two normal packaging attempts failed because the Apple timestamp service was unavailable. The verified local package used a one-shot --timestamp=none codesign invocation; repository/default packaging behavior is unchanged.

verified_mechanisms: The existing opaque Metal surface expands upward to include New Tab; no second surface, command queue or renderer is introduced. Rust aligns the action width with the list viewport, keeping the native scrollbar gutter outside the canvas.
New Tab creates no native title/detail Labels in the Metal backend. Rust emits its plus icon, title, focus/hover appearance and configured shortcut hint, using native title font metrics as input.
Shortcut hints use middle truncation in CoreText; truncation mode participates in the frame fingerprint and bounded text texture cache key.
SetDetail updates the Spec model as well as native Labels, preserving configured shortcut text in the GPU scene. Outer paint invalidations schedule coalesced updates before native rasterization.

A pixel test paints the action at a local origin: native control ink is absent while Metal is visible and present after the native window is hidden. Initial GPU ownership invalidates the previous native fallback record; hide/animation/drawable-failure paths request fresh native fallback paint.

The native regression changes New Tab to Cmd+Shift+U, observes that hint in the submitted scene, physically clicks the action, enters a local URL and verifies exactly one new real tab in the Work profile. The configured shortcut then opens the same blank address workflow without creating a premature tab.
Fractional viewport bounds/clip validation now explicitly translates native list coordinates into the expanded canvas using its submitted screen bounds.
The full matrix retains native input, drag/close, scroll, split/pin/folder state, large-list cache invariants, native fallback animation, sessions, palettes and settings.
measurement_correction: An initial bitmap assertion used the parent-relative child position as the tiny bitmap origin and clipped away its drawing. The helper now temporarily paints the action at (0,0) and restores its bounds; both unchanged paint-state assertions pass.
manual_observations: The verified matching local package displayed the GPU New Tab plus icon, title and Cmd+T hint with the original Unicode split pair.
Clicking New Tab opened the existing blank address palette. A loopback URL created a real Nowa karta GPU page and a new visible row at the end of the scrollable list.
The new row remained visible while the New Tab action stayed fixed above the scrolling list. The native scrollbar remained visible outside the canvas.
The test page was closed; scrolling to the top and selecting the original first pair member restored the 24-tab demo and original split pair. The prototype was closed.
The normal application/profile was not used.
limitations: The local package is signed without a trusted timestamp because the remote service was unavailable; it is a development verification artifact, not a notarized release installer.

Native outer vertical placement, Button/focus/accessibility/action adapters, address palette editing/IME and actual browser commands remain. Rust owns the action interior and width alignment; this is not complete native container removal.
Address pill, workspace heading/footer, split headers/divider and native animation snapshots still require migration.
Bitmap and submitted-scene assertions establish paint routing and content, not a controlled CPU/GPU/physical-presentation speedup or a complete VoiceOver/scale matrix.
No new third-party crate, library or binary framework was added.
